sections.facts: An Ambassador car was purchased by M/s. Karamchand Thapar & Bros. (Coal Sales) Ltd., Delhi in the year 1966 and was transferred to respondent No. 1 United Collieries Ltd., the owners in relation to the North Chirimiri Collieries, and it was, therefore, the owner of the said vehicle. On and from the appointed day, i.e., May 1, 1973, the right, title and interest of the owners in relation to the coal mines specified in the schedule stood transferred to and became vested in the Central Government free from all encumbrances under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973. Immediately after nationalisation, the Deputy Custodian General, Coal Mines Authority Limited, Nagpur addressed a letter dated May 9, 1973 to the Technical Advisor to the North Chirimiri Collieries using the said staff car to hand it over to the custodian. The Managing Director, Western Division, Coal Mines Authority, by an order dated August 9, 1973/1983, directed the respondents to hand over possession of the car failing which they would be liable to prosecution under the Act. Thereupon, respondent No. 1 and the Technical Advisor assailed this order by a petition under Article 226 of the Constitution before the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court. The High Court, purporting to rely on the decision in New Satgram Engineering Works & Anr. v. Union of India, held that whether the staff car should be treated as belonging to the owner of a mine as part of the mine itself raised disputed questions of fact relating to its user to be determined on evidence, discharged the rule, and left the parties to have their rights adjudicated in a civil suit. Feeling aggrieved, the Union of India preferred the appeal by special leave as the question involved affected a large number of cases.
sections.statute: Section 3(1), Section 2(h), Section 2(h)(xi), and Section 2(h)(xii) of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973; Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
sections.argument: The car was not handed over on the plea that it was not used by the Technical Advisor exclusively for the North Chirimiri Collieries but used by him for looking after the multifarious activities of the Thapar Group of industries, which was a composite concern with businesses other than coal mining; therefore, although the car belonged to respondent No. 1, the owners of the North Chirimiri Collieries, it was not a staff car 'belonging to the mine'.
sections.analysis: Parliament, by an enlarged definition of 'mine' in section 2(h) of the Act, has indicated the nature of the properties that vest, and whether a particular asset is taken within the sweep of section 2(h) depends on whether it answers the description given therein. The staff car was undoubtedly a fixed asset of the North Chirimiri Collieries, and belonging to respondent No. 1, the owners in relation to the said mine, being the staff car of the Technical Advisor, was a 'fixed asset' belonging to the mine. 'Fixed assets' in general comprise those assets held for the purpose of conducting a business, in contradistinction to assets held for converting into cash, including real estate, buildings, machinery, etc. The staff car, therefore, fell within the definition of 'mine' under section 2(h)(xii) and vested in the Central Government under section 3(1). Merely because the Technical Advisor was putting the staff car to personal use or for multifarious activities of the Thapar Group of Industries would not alter the true legal position, since subsequent user for a different purpose was not really germane. There is a difference in language between section 2(h)(xi) ('if solely used') and section 2(h)(xii) ('belonging to the owner of a mine, wherever situated'). The observations in New Satgram Engineering Works regarding resolving disputes by a civil suit depending on the nature of user were made in the context of section 2(h)(xi). The present case is clearly covered by section 2(h)(xii) and not section 2(h)(xi); thus, New Satgram Engineering Works is distinguished.
